name: Antares 230+ (retired 2023)

sources.title: Wikipedia: Antares (rocket)
sources.note: 200-series first stage empty 20,600 kg, gross 262,600 kg, thrust 3,844 kN, Isp 311.9 / 339.2 s, burn 215 s; Castor 30XL gross 26,300 kg, propellant 24,200 kg, thrust 474 kN, burn 156 s; payload to LEO 8,000 kg; diameter 3.9 m; launch site MARS LP-0A; 230+ last flew 2 August 2023

notes: Single source, so nothing here is cross-checked. Derived, not published: first-stage propellant = gross - empty (242,000 kg); second-stage dry = gross - propellant (2,100 kg); second-stage Isp = thrust x burn time/ (propellant x g0) = 311.6 s, which treats the quoted MAXIMUM thrust as constant and is therefore an upperestimate for a solid motor. The source gives one first-stage thrust figure (3,844 kN) without saying sea-level or vacuum, so it is used as is rather than averaged. The 8,000 kg figure has no stated orbit. The vehicle is retired; it is in the library as a real cargo-to-ISS launcher with a different pad and latitude from the other two. Modelling conventions (assumptions, not data): first-stage thrust and Isp are the mean of the published sea-level and vacuum values because the simulator has one of each per stage; cd = 0.3 is assumed; area is the circle of the published core diameter; fairing mass and jettison are not modelled.

sim_validation.note: Heaviest payload reaching perigee >= 160 km, due east from mars_lp0a (resolved to +/- 250 kg; pitch program [5.349, 6.742, -8.191, 0.835, 0.584] found by CMA-ES seed 7). Orbit reached: 164 x 173 km, max q 37.9 kPa. Published figure: 8000 kg.
